title: The Most Important Thing On The First Day Of School -school/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that the single most important goal for the first day of school isn't teaching routines or delivering a great academic lesson — it's ensuring that by the time students go home, they already love being in the class. His central claim is that this emotional buy-in is what generates the behavioral leverage that makes every rule and consequence actually matter later on; students who feel lucky to have a particular teacher want to please that teacher and behave for them. The concrete first-day checklist he offers is deliberately simple: smile and greet each student individually, tell a great story, maintain a spirit of humor, get students moving, teach with passion and clarity, and ensure every student experiences some success. He's explicit that this doesn't require elaborate parties or games — it just requires making whatever is already planned genuinely interesting and delivering it warmly. The piece frames this single emotional outcome as the foundation on which the rest of the SCM approach depends.
points: The top first-day priority, above routines or academics, is that students leave already loving being in the class.
That early emotional buy-in is framed as generating the leverage that makes rules and consequences matter later.
The first-day checklist is simple: individual greetings, storytelling, humor, movement, and ensuring every student tastes success.
No elaborate parties or games are required — just genuine warmth and making whatever's already planned interesting.
quotes: When your students leave for home after the first day of school, they must already love being in your class.
Because, when your students feel lucky that you’re their teacher, they’ll want to listen to you, behave for you, and please you.
This is what you want on the first day. To leave your students happily shaken, with a buzzing in their ears and a slow-fading glow from a classroom experience they never expected.
Instead, have fun and be friendly and pleasant from the very first minute.
Make it exceptional and enjoyable. Put yourself in their shoes. Ease their fears. Make them smile.
